penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Actual PRM configuration restoration after a wipe requires hands-on Salesforce expertise to audit, rebuild, and validate settings — this is skilled consulting work, not something Claude can execute autonomously against a live org.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Disaster-recovery engagements are inherently urgent and synchronous — the client needs a human expert available immediately, not an async automated report.

rationale: The buyer is excellent — Salesforce consultants billing client hours have real budget and a specific urgent pain. However, the service being requested (restoring a wiped PRM configuration) is hands-on expert consulting work that cannot be automated: Claude cannot log into a Salesforce org, inspect its state, and rebuild complex PRM configurations autonomously. The disaster-recovery framing also demands synchronous human availability. A lighter adjacent product (e.g. automated config-snapshot or audit reports) scores better on autonomy but loses much of the urgency signal.
solution_plan: This specific disaster-recovery framing cannot be built and maintained autonomously by a solo non-technical operator. The adjacent idea — an automated Salesforce org configuration snapshot/audit service — is more viable but requires Salesforce API integration work beyond standard Claude + Stripe tooling. A non-technical operator cannot set this up without engineering help. If Youval has a Salesforce-savvy developer partner, the adjacent snapshot product is worth a separate evaluation.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy (4 < 7) and buildability_with_ai (5 < 6) build gates. Human-fulfillment and synchronous-human penalties correctly reflect the consulting nature of the service.
